reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output for a clause that meets the fallback; nothing is proposed to the counterparty, so there is no over-flagging risk.

The cited text supports the classification: Section 5a's minimum monthly fee is bounded by Section 13's one-year term with 30-day non-renewal notice, and Section 14 gives Client an at-will termination right ending fees at the end of the month following notice — i.e., commitment confined to the current 12-month term and exitable, with no shortfall/penalty mechanic and no volume cap on Client usage.

The rationale correctly states this sits at the fallback rather than the preferred (pure usage/ordered-services pricing) and appropriately treats the blank dollar amounts and the Section 4/Section 5 cross-reference mismatch as drafting notes rather than deviations, consistent with the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements.
No deterministic check failures; the redline is byte-identical to the originals, as expected for a compliant finding.
